hypothesis: Known training/evaluation leakage and post-freeze mutation can be made fail-closed by a deterministic corpus manifest binding exact, normalized and detection-only leakage hashes, source lineage, provenance, explicit independently assigned semantic-family identity, one corpus-wide semantic-audit receipt, split identity, protected export semantics and one complete manifest root.
strongest_counterhypothesis: A manifest can create false confidence if semantic-family discovery is incomplete, caller-controlled or contaminated, if the bound semantic-audit receipt is not itself verified, if source/cutoff metadata are incomplete, or if the real corpus pipeline bypasses the gate; therefore this mechanism cannot itself establish semantic decontamination or final training-data acceptance.

live_external_evidence.source: Soft Contamination Means Benchmarks Test Shallow Generalization (arXiv:2602.12413)
live_external_evidence.claim_used: semantic duplicates can evade string-space decontamination and materially confound benchmark generalization estimates

live_external_evidence.source: Simulating Training Data Leakage in Multiple-Choice Benchmarks for LLM Evaluation (arXiv:2505.24263)
live_external_evidence.claim_used: controlled leakage changes evaluation reliability and motivates contamination checks before benchmark release

live_external_evidence.source: The Emperor's New Clothes in Benchmarking? (arXiv:2503.16402)
live_external_evidence.claim_used: benchmark reformulation and mitigation strategies do not universally establish contamination-free evaluation
